rows.grounds: Sandhi-fused form of kāmaḥ and candraḥ, naming two figures in the enumeration.
maheśaḥ with enclitic ca, adding another figure to the list.
Proper name of the deity Indra in the nominative.
śaktiḥ with enclitic ca, adding another principle to the list.
Proper name of the goddess Pārvatī in the nominative.

items.question: Which deities and powers complete the enumerated sequence culminating in Pārvatī?
premises: The verse continues a nominative enumeration of divine figures and principles.
Kāma and Candra are named together in a fused form.
Maheśa, Indra, Śakti, and Pārvatī are added to complete the sequence.
items.inference: The sequence is completed by naming Kāma, Candra, Maheśa, Indra, Śakti, and Pārvatī as its final members.
uncertainties: The precise doctrinal role of each named figure within this specific Śrīvidyā enumeration is not fully specified by the verse alone.
items.plain_english: Kāma and Candra, and Maheśa, and Indra, and Śakti, and Pārvatī.
